summary: Source-level localization (CPU, no GPU): where does the tree verify SPINE diverge from native E5 chain op-by-op in OUR OWN kernels (GDN seq tree-scan, conv-fusion, FA2-fork attn, fp8 GEMMs), and the mathematical alignment that makes it bit-exact to native WITHOUT slowing it (no BI/non-fp8). Native E5 runs the same model+fp8 and drifts 7x less, so a clean fast version provably exists — match it.

reads.op: fp8 block-quant GEMMs in the verify forward = GDN out_proj, full-attn self_attn qkv/o_proj, and language-model MLP gate/up/down. (NOT fp8, so excluded: GDN in_proj_a/in_proj_b, conv1d, lm_head, embed_tokens, mtp.fc — all in modules_to_not_convert per /models/qwen3.6-27b-fp8/config.json.) All fp8 linears route through Fp8LinearMethod.apply -> W8A8BlockFp8LinearOp.apply (fp8.py:486-495).
reads.scaleGranularity: PER-ROW (per-token) x PER-128-COL-GROUP for activations; PER-128x128-BLOCK for weights. Activation scheme = DYNAMIC per-token-group, group_shape (1,128) (config.json: activation_scheme=dynamic, act_per_tensor=false, weight_block_size=[128,128]). BATCH-DEPENDENCE VERDICT = NONE (batch-shape-independent AND batch-content-independent). The activation amax that sets each row's fp8 scale is computed over ONLY that single row's 128-element group: _per_token_group_quant_fp8 maps program-id g_id -> row = g_id // groups_per_row, loads only that row's 128 cols, and computes _absmax = tl.max(tl.abs(y)) over those 128 values (fp8_utils.py:635-636,652,658). Grid is launched (M,) with M = x.numel()//group_size (fp8_utils.py:952), one program per (row,group) -- there is NO cross-row reduction. The GEMM (cutlass _C.cutlass_scaled_mm at _custom_ops.py:845, or the triton_scaled_mm / _w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm fallbacks) computes out[m,n] = sum_k a[m,k]*b[k,n]*scale_a[m,k//128]*scale_b[...]: each output row depends ONLY on input row m; M is purely the parallel axis with no M-reduction (cutlass_scaled_mm doc _custom_ops.py:826 scale_a.shape*[1,128]==a.shape; triton_scaled_mm loads scale_a per-row offsets_scale_am triton_scaled_mm.py:70,109,164; block-fp8 triton kernel accumulates over K only, fp8_utils.py:1127-1136, a_s loaded per-row As+offs_am*stride_As_m fp8_utils.py:1122).
reads.divergesYesNo: NO — the fp8 activation/GEMM scaling is RULED OUT as the batch-shape carrier. A spine row gets bit-identical fp8 bytes and bit-identical GEMM output whether it sits in native's 6-row chain or the tree's 9-10-row batch, provided its own input activation values are bit-identical. The PRIME SUSPECT (batch-shape-dependent per-tensor/per-block fp8 scale computed over the larger/branch-containing batch) does NOT exist in this model: it is per-token-group dynamic, not per-tensor, so adding branch rows cannot change a spine row's scale. The only M-dependent knob in the whole path -- the Triton autotune config select `configs[min(configs.keys(), key=abs(x-M))]` (fp8_utils.py:1235), which could pick a different BLOCK_SIZE_K per batch bucket -- is DEAD on GB10: there is no GB10/Spark config json among the 219 tabulated files (only L40S/H100/H200/A100...), so get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs returns None and the kernel uses the default config with BLOCK_SIZE_K = block_size[1] = 128 fixed, independent of M (fp8_utils.py:1232,1240-1247). DeepGEMM (the one path that TMA-pads M) is OFF on GB10: support_deep_gemm() requires capability 90 or family 100 (cuda.py:515-517) and GB10 is family 120, so is_deep_gemm_supported() is False; flashinfer block-fp8 is SM90+ only. VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT does not change the block-quant GEMM math (fp8.py:449-457 calls the SAME w8a8_block_fp8_linear.apply), consistent with the project memory that BI doesn't swap GB10 fp8 GEMMs. Therefore the deep-spine argmax flip enters UPSTREAM of the fp8 GEMM (the per-row INPUT values to out_proj/o_proj/mlp already differ because of the conv prior-window read at fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:797-818 and/or the GDN tree-scan), and the fp8 GEMM faithfully propagates whatever activations it is handed. The o_proj/out_proj divergence is a SYMPTOM, not the source (matches project_fr13_conv_priorwindow_root: conv1d_out diverges 18.375 while h0_state byte-exact; o_proj_out 0.1875 is downstream).
reads.fixIfYes: No fp8-scaling fix is needed or warranted (would not change the result and could only slow things down). Speed-preserving guidance for the follow-up ladder: do NOT touch the fp8 quantizer or add per-row-vs-batch scale alignment -- it is already per-row and already native-matching by construction; any 'compute scale over spine-rows-only' change is a no-op. The real fix lives upstream and is already identified by sibling readers: (1) the conv prior-window bank-row/column selection at fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:797-818 for num_accepted>1 (project_fr13_conv_priorwindow_root); (2) the GDN sequential tree-scan op-order/bf16-cast seams. To USE this fp8 result as a clean instrument: because the GEMM is provably per-row-deterministic, the ladder can capture the fp8 GEMM INPUT (post-conv/post-scan activation row) for the spine row on both arms -- if those input rows are bit-identical the fp8 GEMM output is guaranteed bit-identical, so any o_proj/out_proj output divergence PROVES the input already diverged, cleanly isolating the carrier to the pre-GEMM wiring without ever suspecting fp8. Keep fp8 + current tiling unchanged (zero speed cost).
reads.magnitude: Zero / sub-floor from the fp8 scaling itself for bit-identical input rows. By construction the per-row group scale and the per-row K-reduction are M-invariant, so the fp8-attributable spine divergence for equal inputs = 0.0 bytes (the residual MMA-grouping floor lives in the FA2 attention path, ~1-2 ULP / 1.33e-12 class, NOT here). The observed o_proj_out ~0.1875 and the ~1.9-nat deep-spine argmax flip are INHERITED from the diverged GEMM INPUT (conv1d_out 18.375 upstream), not generated by fp8 scaling. Magnitude carried by fp8 = exactly whatever the upstream input divergence is, passed through linearly; it neither amplifies via a batch-dependent scale nor introduces a new seam.

reads.exactDivergentOp: CONV TAP ROUNDING. Tree path: src/lumo_flywheel_serving/fr13_tree_conv_fused.py:234-235 `prod = window * conv_weights.t().unsqueeze(0)` then `prod_f32 = prod.to(torch.float32)` — window and conv_weights are BOTH bf16, so the elementwise mul produces a bf16 result (each tap product is ROUNDED TO bf16) BEFORE the fp32 cast/accumulation; legacy emulation mirror at fr13_tree_conv_fused.py:417-420 `(window_col.to(bf16)*w.to(bf16)).to(bf16).to(f32)`; selected in the patcher at scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:2489 `fused_tree_conv_taps_acc(...)` (and the legacy per-col mirror at :2502 `_fr11_conv_tap_product` -> :2120 `(x.to(dtype)*w.to(dtype)).to(dtype).to(f32)`). Native path: /tmp/vllm_live_019/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/causal_conv1d.py:1044 (decode kernel `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel`) and :442 (prefill `causal_conv1d_fn`) BOTH do `acc += matrix_x * matrix_w` where matrix_x/matrix_w are bf16 loads (causal_conv1d.py:962-976 weight loads, :986/:992 x loads) and acc is fp32 (:949-953) — Triton promotes bf16*bf16 to an fp32 product (NO intermediate bf16 rounding) and accumulates in fp32. NET: native = acc_f32 += f32(x_bf16*w_bf16) [product kept full fp32]; tree = acc_f32 += f32(bf16(x_bf16*w_bf16)) [product truncated to bf16 first]. The fused docstring's claim 'bf16 mul is fp32-compute + RNE — exact: 8-bit x 8-bit mantissa products fit fp32' (fr13_tree_conv_fused.py:214-215) is the BUG: 8b x 8b mantissa needs up to 16 bits, bf16 keeps only 8, so the .to(bf16) on the product is a lossy RNE that native never applies. The byte-A/B test (tests/test_fr13_tree_conv_fused_byte_ab.py:332-344 T3) validates fused == legacy_tree_conv_taps_acc_reference (the Python emulation) NOT == native causal_conv1d, so it is byte-exact to the WRONG reference and cannot catch this.
reads.irreducibleOrFixable: CONV = FIXABLE (a pure cast-boundary seam, the same class as the FR12 conv intra-A fp32->bf16 fix 79838bb9, just in the opposite direction). ATTENTION (FA2-fork + full-attn) = IRREDUCIBLE within ~2-ULP (MMA fp32 fragment-grouping + online-softmax tile-boundary rescale-count over the wider tree KV; project_fr13_fa2_fork_nocopy_floor 14/16 whole-tree 0.0, 2 single-bf16-ULP in ~1M) — DO NOT GRIND. fp8 GEMMs = NO SEAM (batch-shape-invariant by construction). In src/lumo_flywheel_serving/fr13_tree_conv_fused.py:234, change `prod = window * conv_weights.t().unsqueeze(0)` (bf16*bf16->bf16) to compute the product in fp32: `prod_f32 = window.to(torch.float32) * conv_weights.t().unsqueeze(0).to(torch.float32)` and drop the now-redundant :235 round-trip, keeping the SAME explicit ordered adds at :244-248 (native's static-range tap order is c=0..3 left-acc, which these adds already match). This is a Python-eager elementwise op on a [tree_n,4,5120] window — promoting the mul to fp32 is ~same FLOPs, no extra kernel launch, no fp8 change, no tiling change => NOT slower (conv is a negligible fraction of the 27GB/forward bandwidth-bound decode). Then RE-BIND the byte-A/B test against a native causal_conv1d_update single-row oracle (not the Python emulation) so the gate is bit-exact to the INCUMBENT. ATTENTION: no fix (accept the 2-ULP floor as the user already accepted).
reads.magnitude: CONV: ~1 bf16 ULP per tap at product magnitude. Each of the 4 taps (linear_conv_kernel_dim=4) loses ~8 low mantissa bits; at conv-product magnitudes O(1-10) that is ~2^-8 * |prod| ≈ 0.004-0.04 per tap, ~4 taps accumulating => O(0.01-0.1) error on conv1d_out per channel, then amplified ~32x by the downstream GDN gate 1/rms and compounded over 48 GDN layers => the coherent super-floor deep-spine argmax flips (consistent with the 22-vs-3 flip excess and the project_fr13_conv_priorwindow_root 18.375 episodic spike when the WIRING bug co-fires). This is the '1-bf16-ULP fingerprint' coherently accumulated, NOT sub-floor noise. ATTENTION: 0.0039 max = single-bf16-ULP, ~15x below the E5 self-noise floor ~0.059, no depth growth = rounding/tie-break signature (irreducible). fp8 GEMM: 0 (per-row scale).

The 7x deep-spine flip is consistent with a DIVERGED SCAN INPUT (upstream in_proj fp8 GEMM batch-shape, Reader-4 scope), not a divergent op inside the scan/conv.
reads.exactDivergentOp: Two candidate seams, both KERNEL-codegen (not math): (1) SCAN LAUNCH GEOMETRY — tree: `num_warps=8` at scripts/../fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:1536 (`launch_tree_gdn_prepared`) with module const `BV = 16` at fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:18 and `tl.static_range(0,N_PAD)`/`tl.static_range(0,i)` unroll at fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:459,461; native: `num_warps = 4` at vllm/model_executor/layers/fla/ops/fused_sigmoid_gating.py:227 with `BV = min(next_power_of_2(V),32) = 32` at fused_sigmoid_gating.py:223 and a runtime `for i_t in range(0,T)` loop at fused_sigmoid_gating.py:136. (2) NON-OP (exonerated): the ancestor-reload select `state_i = tl.where(ancestor, tl.sum(tl.where(offs_n==j,h_cache,0.0),axis=0), state_i)` at fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:462-467 is bit-NEUTRAL (sum is h_cache[j]+0.0 = exact). The actual per-node arithmetic at fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:364-382 (`_gdn_node_step`) is OP-FOR-OP identical to native fused_sigmoid_gating.py:144-167 (softplus beta=1.0 reduces to `x<=20.0,log(1+exp(x))`; l2norm; b_q*scale; b_h*=exp(b_g); b_v-=sum(b_h*b_k,1); b_v*=beta; b_h+=b_v*b_k; o=sum(b_h*b_q,1)).

MATH FIX (speed-preserving, fp8/bf16 kept): make the SPINE rows' GEMM use the SAME reduction kernel native uses for its M=6 chain, by pinning the GEMM algorithm to be M-independent for the verify-forward batch sizes rather than letting the heuristic re-bucket on M=9-10. Two concrete, no-slowdown levers, in order:
(1) Pin the bf16 GEMM algo: set the cuBLAS/cublasLt algo (or torch backend) so the verify forward always dispatches the SAME kernel/tiling for M in {6..16}; the heuristic only re-picks because M crosses a bucket boundary — forcing the M=6 winner for M=9-10 is the SAME kernel, SAME fp8/bf16, same FLOPs, zero added launches (a tree batch of 9-10 rows is already smaller than a prefill, so the M=6 kernel is comfortably efficient at M=10 => not slower; if anything the chain-tuned kernel is the one that was speed-validated). For fp8: confirm the path is cutlass_scaled_mm (_custom_ops.py:845, M is the pure parallel axis, no M-reduction) — if so the fp8 GEMM is already M-invariant by construction (per FP8 reader); then the carrier is bf16-only and the fix is bf16-only.
(2) If (1) can't fully pin (cuBLAS heuristic opaque), the deterministic-but-still-fast fallback is to route ONLY the verify-forward bf16 in_proj/MLP through a fixed-tile Triton GEMM with the same K-reduction tiling native uses (one config, no autotune-by-M) — keeps bf16, one kernel, deterministic across M.

WHY IT KEEPS fp8/SPEED: no quantizer change (fp8 act scale is already per-token-group and native-matching — touching it is a proven no-op); no batch-invariant kernel; no non-fp8 kernel; the tree batch (9-10 rows) is strictly smaller than a normal prefill so reusing native's chain-tuned GEMM kernel is at worst neutral and removes a heuristic re-pick. The only change is forcing algo-determinism across the small M-window the verify forward actually uses.
